# U13 — Escapes and Identities as analyses; stack, identity, isolate and demand as plain passes

Mandatory findings: F-round-2

## Permitted outcome

1. **`idr::Escapes`**, an analysis under `INC/Analysis/Escapes.h`:
   which boxes may outlive their frame, as one sparse backward dataflow
   analysis on the solver over the whole module, and which functions
   may have more than one frame live at a time (C2.1). Mandatory.
2. **`idr::Identities`**, an analysis under `INC/Analysis/Identities.h`:
   the functions that give back an argument, the greatest fixpoint over
   the module, keyed by function name (C2.1). Mandatory.
3. **`idr-stack`**, a `ModuleOp` pass in `IdrSmallPasses` that reads
   `Escapes` and `Layouts` and writes the `idr.stack` mark through
   `IdrDialect::StackAttrHelper` (C1.3, C2.2). Mandatory.
4. **`idr-identity`**, an `::idr::FuncOp` pass that reads `Identities`
   through the parent and makes each call of such a function its
   argument (C1.3). Mandatory.
5. **`idr-isolate`** and **`idr-demand`**, `ModuleOp` passes unchanged in
   meaning, on `idr.func`, `idr.call` and `idr.return`, as plain `.cpp`
   (C1.3, C6.6). Mandatory.
6. **The four old directories deleted**: `IDR/Stack`, `IDR/Identity`,
   `IDR/Isolate`, `IDR/Demand`, whole. Mandatory.
7. **F-round-2 stated and bounded.** `Identities` as an analysis is the
   whole of this packet's answer to F-round-2; the five deadness
   computations stay five. Mandatory; the rest of that finding is
   deferred, not done here.

Consumer adaptations: none outside the write set. The pipeline and the
round are U14's and U04's; the fixtures are U21's and U22's; the hub text
this lane needs is reported, not written.

## Fixed decisions

- **The library.** `IdrSmallPasses` is four `.cpp` files, one per pass:
  `IDR/Transforms/Stack/Stack.cpp`, `IDR/Transforms/Identity/Identity.cpp`,
  `IDR/Transforms/Isolate/Isolate.cpp`, `IDR/Transforms/Demand/Demand.cpp`.
  The two analyses are `IdrAnalysis` units: `IDR/Analysis/Escapes.cpp`
  and `IDR/Analysis/Identities.cpp`, with the split the Escalate section
  names when a unit passes 400 lines. Each pass header
  (`INC/Transforms/Stack.h`, `Identity.h`, `Isolate.h`, `Demand.h`)
  holds its `GEN_PASS_DECL_IDR<NAME>` define and the include of
  `idr/Transforms/Passes.h.inc`, nothing else; each pass `.cpp` holds the
  `GEN_PASS_DEF_IDR<NAME>` define as today's `Pass.cc` files do
  (`IDR/Stack/Pass.cc:6-9`). Every `.cpp` includes `idr/IR/IdrDialect.h`
  first among ours (C1.1).
- **No module, no partition, no `import`, no state across runs.** No
  symbol table is constructed: `idr-stack` and `idr-isolate` take
  `getAnalysis<SymbolTable>()`; the analyses take
  `am.getAnalysis<SymbolTable>()` in their constructors. No lookup goes
  through a scope chain or a memo.
- **`Escapes` is one solve per module.** The parameter summaries, the
  cons and the loops are answered by one `DataFlowSolver` run over the
  module in the analysis's constructor, kept as a member so that
  `mayEscape` reads its states. The worklist over callers
  (`Escape.cppm:171-187`) and the cache keyed by function and innermost
  loop (`:97-99`, `:190-199`) go: the solver's fixpoint is the least
  solution the worklist computed, and the lattice below carries what
  the cache keyed on.
- **Escape's lattice.** For every SSA value whose runtime type holds
  cells (`Escape.cppm:113-118`), a product of two components, `shallow`
  and `deep` (`:4-9`, `:68-71`), each a `Reach` of three parts:
  `escapes` (the reference reaches a use that lets it go), `tailCalled`
  (a call in tail position of the value's function, of a function on
  that function's cycle, takes it: `:283-290`), and `loops`, the set of
  `scf.while` ops whose terminators forward it (`:244-250`). Bottom is
  nothing. `meet` and `join` (the `Lattice` template needs both) are the
  same union of every part, then `shallow` takes `deep`'s parts: what is
  reachable from a value includes its own reference (`:210-211`). Both
  are monotone; the solve ends. A value that is not a box has one
  component, `deep`, as `node` collapses today (`:154-156`): the
  transfer writes and reads `deep` for it.
- **Escape's transfer**, backward, from results to operands, by the
  rules of `Escape.cppm:241-296`, for operands that hold cells:
  - `idr.field`: `deep` takes the result's `deep`; `shallow` nothing.
    `idr.tag`: nothing.
  - The scrutinee of `idr.match`, which the framework hands to
    `visitBranchOperand` because it is not forwarded: `shallow` is exit
    when the scrutinee's quantity is one (`:265-267`), else nothing;
    `deep` takes the `deep` of every argument of every case region, read
    with `getOrCreateFor` at the point after the match.
  - The fields of `idr.con`: `shallow` and `deep` take the result's
    `deep` (`:273`).
  - `arith.select`, `idr.lin.enter`, `idr.lin.use`: each component takes
    the result's same component (`:276-278`).
  - `idr.call` of an `idr.func` with a body: each operand component's
    `escapes` takes the matching component's `escapes` of the callee's
    parameter (`:291-292`) and nothing else of that lattice; when the
    call is in tail position and the callee is on the function's cycle,
    `tailCalled` is set (`:288-290`). No such function or no body: exit
    (`:280-282`). This is the interprocedural rule; the parameter's own
    lattice is its summary, and the solver's dependency on it re-runs
    the call when it grows.
  - `idr.return`: exit for every operand (`:21-22`).
  - A terminator whose parent is an `scf.while` (`scf.condition`,
    `scf.yield`): the framework's forwarding to the successor inputs, and
    the while added to `loops` of both components of each forwarded
    operand (`:244-250`).
  - `idr.yield` of a match: the framework's forwarding to the match's
    results. `visitNonControlFlowArguments`: nothing.
  - Every other use, `visitCallOperand` included (`idr.apply` resolves
    to no callable): exit (`:295`). `setToExitState` sets `escapes` on
    both components.
- **Where the base's rule differs, `visit` is overridden.** The abstract
  backward class derives a return's operands from the known callers'
  results and a call's operands from the callee's whole parameter
  lattice (`SparseAnalysis.h:461-468` and the pinned `SparseAnalysis.cpp`).
  Neither is this analysis's rule: a returned cell is in a frame that is
  gone whatever the caller does with it, and `tailCalled` must not cross
  a call. So the analysis overrides `visit(ProgramPoint *)`
  (`SparseAnalysis.h:415`): for the op before the point, when it is
  `idr.return` or `idr.call`, the rules above and no call of the base;
  when it is a terminator of an `scf.while`, the base's `visit` and then
  the loop tag; otherwise the base's `visit`. Operand lattices come from
  `getLatticeElement`, other lattices from `getOrCreateFor` at the point
  after the op, updates through `propagateIfChanged` or the base's
  `meet`. `DeadCodeAnalysis` is not loaded: the one place the base reads
  predecessors is the return rule, which is overridden.
- **The frame question at query time.** `mayEscape(con)` keeps
  `repeating` (`Escape.cppm:124-140`): the regions from the con to its
  function are one block each and belong to matches or whiles, else the
  answer is true. Then the con's result lattice: true when `shallow` has
  `escapes` or `tailCalled`, or its `loops` meets the whiles on the way
  up. No lattice: true.
- **The cycles are private to `Escapes`.** The call graph of
  `Recursion.cppm:41-85` (a call names its callee, a self call in tail
  position is no edge, a function with an `idr.apply` reaches every
  function whose symbol is used other than as a callee) is built in the
  constructor before the solve, and its components come from
  `llvm::scc_iterator` over an index graph with a `GraphTraits`
  specialization, as `IDR/Graph/Scc.cppm:14-57` does today; those lines
  are duplicated into `Escapes.cpp` as glue. `Escapes::recursive(FuncOp)`
  is public (the frame budget needs it); `together` is private.
- **The tail-position test** (`IDR/Graph/InTailPosition.cppm:18-27`,
  with `idr.return` for `func.return`) is a static in `Escapes.cpp`.
- **`idr-stack`** is `Mark.cppm:55-81` as a pass body: `getAnalysis<Escapes>()`,
  `getAnalysis<idr::Layouts>()`, `getAnalysis<SymbolTable>()`; a
  `StackAttrHelper` from the dialect; every mark removed through the
  helper before deciding (`:58`), then set through it (`:76`). The
  limits 256, 1024 and 64 keep their values and their comments
  (`:14-17`, `:37-39`). The budget asks `escapes.recursive(fn)`; the size
  is `layouts.box(lookupCtor(symbols, con.getCtor())).size` by the names
  `INC/IR/Layout.h` and `INC/IR/Symbols.h` give. The pass fails with the
  internal error of C2.0 when a required analysis is absent, and with
  the failure `Layouts` reports, if `Layout.h` reports one, as
  `Pass.cc:18-19` does today. It calls `markAllAnalysesPreserved()`: a
  mark is read by `idr-lower` and by `idr.con`'s effects, by no analysis
  of C2.1. `numBoxes` and `numCells` stay.
- **`Identities`** is `Identities.cppm:54-109` as a class: the
  candidates (`:33-47`), one record per function (today's `Rebuilds`),
  the callers map, the worklist that only drops assumptions, and the
  result as `DenseMap<StringAttr, unsigned>`, read by
  `std::optional<unsigned> givesBack(StringAttr function) const`. Keyed
  by name because a function pass has a call's callee name and no
  operation. The record reads a callee's facts through `idr::FuncOp`'s
  generated `getEffects()` (C2.2): a function the module lacks, without
  a body or without `effects` may do anything, as `IDR/Facts/Of.cppm:14-24`
  says; `returns` is the absence of `diverge` in the attribute's value.
  `isInvalidated` returns true unless `Identities` and `SymbolTable` are
  preserved.
- **No erased value exists** (C6.1, C10). In the record, "a constructor
  whose fields are all erased" (`Rebuilds.cppm:253-254`) becomes "a
  constructor with no fields"; the erased-field skip (`:611-612`) and the
  erased test among candidates (`Identities.cppm:44`) go. Nothing else of
  the rules changes.
- **`idr-identity`** reads `getCachedParentAnalysis<Identities>()` and
  fails its function with an internal error naming the analysis when it
  is absent (C2.0's rule for the symbol table, applied). The rewrite is
  one `OpRewritePattern<idr::CallOp>` holding the analysis: a call whose
  callee gives back argument `i` is replaced by `heldAs(rewriter, loc,
  args[i], result type)` (`Identities.cppm:136-142`), applied with
  `walkAndApplyPatterns` over the function (C2.0). The pattern counts
  its rewrites into `numCalls`; a function with none calls
  `markAllAnalysesPreserved()`.
- **`idr-identity` erases no function.** It cannot: it sees one function
  and the callee may still be named by a closure. The function stays and
  `symbol-dce`, the round's last step (C3.2), erases it once nothing
  names it, as today (`Identities.cppm:119-121`).
- **F-round-2.** Making `Identities` an analysis read by a function pass
  is the step this packet takes on F-round-2: the identity question is
  computed once per round and applied in parallel, and nothing else of
  the five deadness computations (`remove-dead-values`, `symbol-dce`,
  `idr-identity`, canonicalize's dead-op erasure,
  `idr-returned-arguments`) moves. Merging them into one fixpoint is
  deferred, to be measured after C4 lands, and is not begun here.
- **`idr-isolate`** is `Isolate.cppm:64-139` on the new ops: the bodies
  collected innermost first, each outlined into an `idr.func` built with
  the generated builder of C1.2's `Idr_FuncOp`, `setPrivate()`,
  `setTotal(true)`, `setBreakLast(enclosing.getBreakLast())`, inserted
  through the `SymbolTable` from `getAnalysis<SymbolTable>()` at the
  position `:115-117` chooses; its yield becomes `idr.return`; the names
  `<f>$lam<n>` and `<f>$delay<n>` and the location rule (`:105-110`)
  stay; `makeRegionIsolatedFromAbove` with the constant predicate
  (`:87-91`) stays. The order innermost first is the pass's meaning
  (`T/idr/isolate/nested.mlir`), which no pattern driver's walk gives, so
  the collect-then-rewrite loop stays as it is. Outlined something:
  `markAnalysesPreserved<SymbolTable>()`, since every insertion went
  through it; nothing to outline: `markAllAnalysesPreserved()`.
- **`idr-demand`** is `Demand.cppm:24-111` on the new ops. It reads the
  grades `idr-rc` wrote into the types (`:97`) and the ops it placed
  (`idr.reuse`, `idr.take`, `idr.dup`, `idr.borrow`); it reads no
  analysis. Should the check come to need one, the only names are
  `idr::Borrows` and `idr::Exclusivity` of `INC/Analysis/Ownership.h`,
  through `getAnalysis`. The option `in-place`, the message
  `unsupported (uniqueness)` (`:68-70`) and the reporting rule (`:101-109`)
  are unchanged. It always calls `markAllAnalysesPreserved()` (`Pass.cc:21`).
- **Names.** `idr::Escapes`, `idr::Identities`, in namespace `idr`;
  the lattice, the dataflow analysis class, the cycles, the record and
  the parts are private to their `.cpp` or nested in the public class.

  pass as C1.3 says and the analysis for whoever computes it; the ruling
  changes only the producer and the fixture's pipeline spelling.

  list of the dialect", while C2.2 and C4 keep `idr.stack` as a

    pass, analysis, library, file, option and rule names are fixed
    there. Consume them by name. Never redeclare one under another
    spelling.

    `proposals/0015-cutover-swarm/findings.md` that carry your evidence.
    Read them; they hold the `path:line` anchors.
  - Path roots: `FI` is `foreign/idr`, `INC` is `foreign/idr/include/idr`,
    `IDR` is `foreign/idr/lib`, `CS` is `compiler/src/IdrisMLIR`, `RT` is
    `runtime`, and `T` is `tests`.
- **No coding until dispatched.** This file is a dispatch for a swarm
  the owner has not launched yet. Do not act on it unless the
  coordinator hands it to you as your assignment.

  deleted and every `.cpp` written at the same time, by 22 other lanes,
  and the coordinator writes the hubs (C1) and every `CMakeLists.txt`.

  - Write against the packet text.
  - Report `Verification: NotRun (swarm policy)` for what you did not

- **The hubs are the coordinator's.** Never edit these:
  - `INC/IR/IdrOps.td`, `INC/IR/IdrPlatformOps.td`,
    `INC/Transforms/Passes.td`;
  - every `CMakeLists.txt`, `CMakePresets.json`, `.gitmodules`,

## Binding rules

1. Do exactly the assigned obligations and necessary consumer adaptations within the exclusive write set. Every changed hunk, new file, dependency or abstraction must map to a named obligation. If the contract cannot be completed within those writes, report the exact missing seam; do not silently widen scope.
2. Add no unsolicited features, frameworks, generic helpers, configuration knobs, retries, telemetry, documentation, dependencies, formatting sweeps or neighboring cleanup. Elegance means completing the selected representation and deleting its named predecessor, not opening another project.
3. Do not be afraid to duplicate reading, investigation, reasoning or small packet-local non-authoritative implementation glue. Do not wait for a sibling merely to avoid that duplication or introduce a shared helper that creates a false dependency. Reuse already-landed repairs; duplicated investigation does not mean rebuilding working mechanisms.
4. Authoritative schemas, vocabularies, identities and business facts still have exactly one owner. Never duplicate them, create competing implementations or write concurrently to another owner's file. Duplicate effort is allowed; duplicate authority and overlapping writes are not.
5. Finish the bounded deliverable, report changed paths against obligations plus checks actually run and unresolved seams, then return control. Do not roam into another packet, manufacture work to maintain swarm headcount, or build a reporting/coordination platform.
6. User steering goes through the coordinator into the affected packet only. The coordinator corrects an architectural contradiction in the canonical contract and re-dispatches the affected lane. No lane stops for it.
